title: The name Ardenna
text:
Hey Claude, how do you pronounce Ardenna?  

"Ardenna" is pronounced ar-DEN-uh (with the stress on the middle syllable).
It's the genus name for shearwaters - those incredible long-distance seabirds that spend most of their lives at sea, gliding low over the waves. A fitting name for a bluewater cruising yacht!
author: Doug

title: Looking for a 1,500nm logbook entry?
text:
We will be heading south this autumn to the Dominican Republic and are looking for crew to join the fun. This is not a potential or a maybe, but a confirmed passage departing Newport for Puerto Bahía Marina in Samaná, DR, this November 2026.

Over Halloween weekend, we will meet with other members of the Bluewater Sailing Club in Newport, RI, to prep, plan, and commune before heading out to sea together. Specifically, we will be at a dock at the Newport Yachting Center October 30 – November 1, leaving (weather permitting) for what will be a 9–12 day passage directly to the DR.

Are you interested in joining us? This will be a fun offshore passage with a wide range of weather, currents, and marine life. We will embrace the cold New England weather with layers of wool under our bibs and hoodies while enjoying the warmth of the full-boat Webasto hydronic heater, knowing it won’t be long before it is almost too hot.

Leaving Newport, we will head East to cut the Gulf Stream and then start a straight shot South, taking Bermuda to port. Within a few days, the weather will warm, and we will ditch the wool and start washing the salt off our sunnies. A few more days after that, you will need sunscreen for your legs as shorts become the order of the day. Once we get South of Florida, it will just be hot!

Weather windows open and close quickly in New England in autumn, so some flexibility regarding the Samaná arrival will be needed; however, the total trip should take between 8–12 days. We greatly prefer to sail but will motor to keep things moving, charge batteries, and make hot water. Everyone will have their own bunk and locker, and a freshwater shower every day or two. We will pay for food, customs, visas, and transportation to the Santo Domingo airport. You will handle the trip to Newport (we can pick you up at Boston Logan) and the trip home from the DR.
author: Doug
